definition: A male performer who streams sexual or erotic content live via webcam for a paying online audience.
notes: English loanword used in Polish internet culture; male counterpart to camgirl; recognized primarily by younger, internet-active demographics; used without morphological adaptation in Polish.

definition: Subscription content platform used generically in Polish to mean online explicit content creation and digital sex work.
notes: Used generically in Polish — 'założyć OnlyFans' (to start an OnlyFans) has become a general idiom for entering the online sex content industry regardless of platform; morphologically invariant in Polish.

definition: Polish phrase for 'adult content creator'; a neutral-to-euphemistic self-descriptor for a person who produces and sells explicit sexual content online.
notes: Direct calque of the English 'adult content creator'; preferred on social media and in professional self-presentation to avoid platform content moderation bans; 'treści dla dorosłych' literally means 'content for adults'.

definition: Brand name used generically in Polish to mean online pornography or pornographic streaming sites broadly.
notes: Metonymic generalization in Polish internet usage; 'oglądać PornHub' simply means to watch online pornography regardless of platform; reflects near-universal name recognition; used as a generic noun and verb base in informal register.

definition: Sexual trolling; the act of making deliberately offensive, sexually provocative, or harassing comments online for shock value, amusement, or to distress others.
notes: Polish calque of English 'trolling' + the adjective 'seksualny'; covers both edgelord shock humor and targeted sexual harassment in online spaces; the concept maps imperfectly to edgelord as it can involve targeted victims rather than general provocation.

definition: Non-consensual distribution of intimate or sexually explicit images of a person, typically by a former partner as retaliation.
notes: English phrase used unchanged in Polish discourse; criminalized in Poland under Article 191a of the Criminal Code since 2017 (up to 3 years imprisonment); the Polish equivalent 'pornografia zemsty' exists but 'revenge porn' dominates everyday usage.

definition: AI-synthesized pornographic video or image depicting a real person without their consent, created using deep learning face-swap technology.
notes: Hybrid term: 'deepfake' borrowed intact from English, 'porno' is the Polish colloquial form; technically distinct from revenge porn (synthetic vs real footage) but legally and ethically overlapping; Polish criminal law coverage is still developing as of 2026.

definition: Polish internet slang for sex or a sexual encounter, used analogously to 'przelecieć kogoś' (to bang/screw someone) with a similar conquest framing.
notes: Niche internet slang; the associated term 'przelecieć' (literally 'to fly over') is well-established Polish crude slang for having sex with conquest framing; 'neta' appears to be a coded or shortened derivative used in specific online communities; very low mainstream penetration.

definition: Sin; the primary Polish Catholic term for moral transgression, widely used in sexual contexts to mean sexual sin or violation of chastity norms.
notes: The generic Polish word for sin; in Catholic sexual discourse it functions as a meta-category encompassing all sexual transgressions; mapping to 'fornication' is approximate — fornication is one paradigmatic referent among many; near-universal recognition in Poland's majority-Catholic culture; the phrase 'to grzech' (that is a sin) is a commonplace moral judgment.

definition: Impure sin; the standard Polish Catholic catechetical term for sexual sins specifically, including fornication, masturbation, homosexual acts, and other violations of chastity.
notes: Direct phrase from Polish Catholic catechesis; 'nieczysty' means impure/unclean; covers a broader range of sexual sins than fornication alone; routinely taught in Polish religious education (lekcje religii) and used in confessional contexts; recognition lower among younger secular Poles.

definition: Carnal sin or sin of the flesh; a Catholic theological term for sins arising from bodily desire, specifically sexual sins framed as the corruption of the body.
notes: Theologically frames sexual sin as rooted in the carnal (cielesny = bodily) nature; contrasted with sins of the spirit; slightly more literary and theological in register than 'grzech nieczysty'; maps to 'concupiscence' as both concepts locate the sinful tendency in the inherited carnal appetite.

definition: Impurity; the Catholic moral concept of sexual uncleanness, denoting the state of having committed or being disposed toward sexual sin.
notes: 'Nieczysty' literally means unclean; central to Polish Catholic sexual shame discourse; appears in catechism, confessional language, and moral theology; also has non-sexual meanings (physical uncleanliness, ritual impurity) making the sexual sense context-dependent; the abstract noun form used to describe a condition of moral-sexual corruption.

definition: Archaic Polish term for lewdness, wantonness, or sexual licentiousness; a moralistic condemnation of uninhibited or promiscuous sexual behavior.
notes: Now largely obsolete; found in 19th-century Polish religious and literary texts and in older Bible translations (particularly Protestant); 'wszetecznica' (a lewd woman) was a common derived form; recognized mainly by older, educated, or religiously informed Poles; effectively replaced by 'rozwiązłość' and 'lubieżność' in contemporary usage.

definition: Promiscuity, dissoluteness, or sexual licentiousness; a Polish moral condemnation of having many sexual partners or living a sexually unrestrained life.
notes: 'Rozwiązły' (the adjective) means dissolute or licentious; commonly used in Catholic moral discourse and conservative journalism; retains a clearly disapproving tone even in secular contexts; slightly more formal than everyday speech; often applied to women with heightened social force.

definition: Shamelessness; the absence of sexual or moral shame, specifically behaving in ways that violate Catholic norms of decency without remorse or inhibition.
notes: 'Bez' (without) + 'wstyd' (shame); the adjective 'bezwstydny' (shameless) is the more common form; used both in Catholic moral discourse and in everyday condemnation; the framing of public decency violation as rooted in lacking shame is characteristic of honor-shame culture; slightly more emotional and condemnatory in tone than 'nieczystość'.

definition: Sexual abstinence or continence; the deliberate restraint from sexual activity, presented as a virtue in Catholic moral theology and natural family planning discourse.
notes: Formal theological register; also used in non-sexual contexts (e.g., abstinence from alcohol); in sexual discourse refers specifically to the virtue of continence; prominent in Polish Catholic catechesis, NFP (natural family planning) advocacy, and pre-marital preparation courses.

definition: Purity or chastity; the Catholic virtue of sexual purity, encompassing abstinence before marriage, fidelity in marriage, and freedom from sexual sin.
notes: The primary Polish word for both physical cleanliness and moral purity; in sexual contexts denotes chastity specifically; 'czystość serca' (purity of heart) is a major Polish Catholic spiritual concept; maps approximately to 'sexual_abstinence' though czystość is a broader virtue covering thought and intention as well as act; near-universal recognition as a common word with a heightened theological register in Catholic discourse.

definition: Virginity; the state of not having had sexual intercourse, treated as a moral, social, and religious value in Polish Catholic culture.
notes: Near-universal recognition; concept maps approximately to 'defloration' since no registry entry names the virgin state itself, only its loss; 'zachować dziewictwo' (to preserve one's virginity) was a dominant norm in Polish Catholic upbringing for generations; carries both physical and spiritual dimensions in Catholic discourse.

definition: Virgin; a woman who has not had sexual intercourse; also the title of the Virgin Mary ('Najświętsza Dziewica'), giving the word profound religious resonance in Polish culture.
notes: Extremely common; carries simultaneously secular and deeply religious weight due to Marian devotion ('Dziewica Maryja'); the male form 'dziewiczak' exists but is far less culturally charged; maps approximately to 'defloration' as the registry lacks a concept entry for the virgin state itself.

definition: Virtue; in Polish usage most commonly connotes sexual virtue or chastity specifically, making 'stracić cnotę' (to lose one's virtue) the standard Polish euphemism for losing virginity.
notes: The general word for virtue but in everyday Polish usage it is most commonly understood to mean chastity or virginity specifically; 'cnotliwy' (virtuous) in sexual contexts means chaste; the narrowing of virtue to sexual virtue reflects the centrality of chastity in Polish Catholic moral culture.

definition: Loss of virtue; the standard Polish Catholic euphemism for losing one's virginity, framing the event as an irreversible moral diminishment.
notes: Nominal phrase; 'utrata' means loss (irreversible); frames virginity as a virtue that, once lost, cannot be recovered; carries strong moral weight in Catholic contexts; used across generations in both formal discourse and everyday speech; the euphemistic framing avoids naming the sexual act directly.

definition: To lose one's virtue; the standard Polish verbal euphemism for losing one's virginity, carrying the same Catholic moral framing as 'utrata cnoty'.
notes: Verbal phrase equivalent of 'utrata cnoty'; 'stracić' means to lose irreversibly; used across generations and registers; the moral-religious framing is implicit but widely understood even in secular contexts; the most common way to express first intercourse in a non-crude register in Polish.

definition: Modesty; the Catholic virtue of sexual and behavioral restraint, including modest dress, language, and deportment, presented as an ideal especially for women.
notes: Very common Polish word with both general and specifically sexual-moral usage; in Catholic sexual discourse 'skromność' is a central feminine virtue covering dress, conduct, and sexual restraint; maps approximately to 'sexual_conservatism' though skromność is a positive ideal rather than a conservative political stance.

definition: A modest woman; the Polish Catholic archetype of a woman who embodies sexual restraint, modest dress, and chastity norms.
notes: A phrase rather than a single lexical item; 'skromna kobieta' functions as a culturally loaded social archetype contrasting with 'rozwiązła kobieta' (licentious woman); used approvingly in conservative and Catholic contexts and sometimes ironically by more secular speakers; the gendering is significant — 'skromny mężczyzna' (modest man) carries far less moral weight.

definition: Public decency or sexual morality; the Polish legal and moral standard of acceptable sexual conduct, also a formal legal term in obscenity and indecency offenses.
notes: 'Obraza obyczajności publicznej' (offense against public morality) is a formal charge under Polish administrative and criminal law; 'obyczajność' names the positive standard that indecency violates; formal register recognized primarily by educated speakers and those familiar with legal or Catholic moral discourse; recognition has declined among younger secular demographics.
